title: Be human and fallible: why sincere, specific personality beats sterile corporate polish
summary: Jason Cohen argues customers now expect providers to try hard, care, and treat them well when things inevitably break, and they forgive sincere human error but turn adversarial toward sterile corporate behavior. He offers practical ways to find your voice and warns that a strong persona will alienate some people while making the rest love you.

principles.text: Customers forgive sincere human error but grow adversarial and distrustful toward sterile corporate relationships.
principles.quote: People readily forgive sincere human error, but become adversarial and distrustful with the typical, sterile customer/provider relationship.

principles.text: The modern expectation isn't zero mistakes; it's that you care and respond well when you inevitably screw up.
principles.quote: The new attitude is not "Those assholes better not *ever* screw up," but rather "I expect them to try hard, to care, and to treat me well *when* they inevitably screw up."

principles.text: Earn forgiveness through ongoing effort, learning from mistakes, and a culture of excellence, not a faux-heartfelt crisis apology.
principles.quote: You're learning from your mistakes, evidenced by problems tending towards the esoteric, and by explaining in your apology what steps you've taken to avoid this and similar classes of error.

principles.text: Find your voice by criticizing others, deciding what you are not, and copying something you love as a rough draft.
principles.quote: It's easy to identify corporate stuff that pisses you off; use that to decide both what not to do and what to do instead.

principles.text: Every strong decision alienates some people while thrilling others; be strong, specific, and honest anyway.
principles.quote: every strong decision you make will necessarily alienate many people even while it's thrilling others.

principles.text: Having no persona gives nobody a reason to get excited, tolerate faults, or tell friends, so be soulful.
principles.quote: Then why would anyone get excited about you? Why would they put up with your faults? Why would they tell their friends about you?
